authors: Erin Rae Toppe; prepared with Claude
claim: Indus inscriptions found abroad (Mesopotamia, Iran, the Gulf, Oman, Central Asia) contain a larger share of adjacent sign pairs never seen in home Indus texts than texts from small home sites do, scored the same way.
basis: results/abroad_pairs_scouting.md: exploration, 13 abroad texts 0.63 vs 230 small-home-site texts 0.45, +0.19, p 0.038. Follows Hunter (1932), Parpola (1994: 309) and Laursen (2010: 116-117), who report that most Gulf-seal sequences are not paralleled in the Indus Valley.
small_site_rule: home sites with fewer than 60 exploration texts (deduplicated, damaged kept)
test_texts: abroad and small-home-site texts of 2+ signs from the export's locked holdout and the held-out-from-export set; never analysed for this question
note: Registered before any rate was computed on the test texts. Only counts of test texts by site group were looked at (--dry). Not part of the BH family of the new-set batch; reported on its own.
